question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/b5ea4fcb15db81b35a8a6e399cc3df734fc1dd41afe42799b8ca2a39734996cb.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x=-\frac{10}{y}$ and $x=y-7$ for $y\in [2,5]$ is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the line $x=-1.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
Let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/987999e84c2b22c8b90ecb0381518e7504d0b792ecebb067a7221653422b3e89.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=-\frac{10}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=y-7.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as a difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y-7.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/f8c250c5fbf20980050a1e86f4ac5c91bff7b24bfc7ce5394f33c87703139026.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(-1)-(y-7)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[6-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=-\frac{10}{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226182/assets/64b440be918c616eb07f05f7f09cb8e14ed649f677afc5f40f66f47ec34ed87e.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\,(-1)-(-\frac{10}{y})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[6-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{2}^{5}({[6-y]}^{2}-{[\frac{10}{y}-1]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
